edition.sessionCovered: Wed, Nov 4 (Democrats projected to win House · oil slides on Iran peace hopes · US strikes Qeshm Island)
edition.stripNote: Wed 4 Nov. Democrats projected to win House. Cooper flips NC Senate. Oil slides — Brent $104, WTI $96. Gold volatile ($3,893–$3,953 range). US strikes Qeshm Island during peace talks. NFP Fri.
edition.scoreboardCaption: Wed 4 Nov vs Tue 3 Nov close. Ranked best to worst.
edition.commodleHint: Democrats are projected to recapture the _____ of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections

overview: Oil extended its post-crash decline on Wednesday as Iran peace hopes continued to weigh on the risk premium, even as the US carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of November 3. Brent eased to $103.89, down 1.4% from Tuesday's $105.38, while WTI slipped to $95.60. Tehran described the exchanges as 'intensive' but Foreign Minister Araghchi said on November 2 that 'the ball is in the US court,' insisting Washington must lift the naval blockade, return frozen assets, and halt hostilities before the strait can reopen. Iran's Navy claimed an 11th oil tanker caught fire near the strait from a sea mine, contradicting US Central Command's assertion that main transit routes remain clear. Trump said a deal 'could happen' but also noted the US still had targets to address. OPEC+ continues to hold December quotas unchanged, with the November 29 session to set 2027 targets.

Gold had its most volatile session of the month, touching an intraday low of $3,893 before recovering to settle near $3,935 as early midterm results showed Democrats on track to win back the House of Representatives. Roy Cooper flipped North Carolina's Senate seat for Democrats, but overall Senate control remained undecided with Alaska's ranked-choice vote and Maine's tight Collins-Jackson race still outstanding. Silver eased to $49.85, platinum fell to $1,437, and palladium continued its slide to $940 — extending its 16-month low. Copper held at $6.41 per pound, with LME inventories tight but macro uncertainty capping gains. Bitcoin dipped below $77,000 as post-Binance hack outflows persisted and election uncertainty weighed on risk appetite. Lithium carbonate fell to ¥93,800 in China, down from ¥97,500, as oversupply concerns intensified. Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report (consensus 65K) is the next macro catalyst ahead of the December 8–9 FOMC meeting.

watchItems.title: Democrats projected to win House — Senate control still undecided
watchItems.text: Early midterm results show Democrats on track to recapture the House of Representatives, with Roy Cooper flipping North Carolina's Senate seat. However, overall Senate control remains uncertain — Alaska's ranked-choice voting and Maine's tight Collins-Jackson race could take days to resolve. A Democratic House would likely resist new military authorization for Iran and could pursue oversight of the Binance hack response. Crypto-backed PACs spent approximately $170 million in the cycle, and the composition of the new Congress will shape the regulatory landscape for digital assets.

watchItems.title: US strikes Qeshm Island while talking peace — escalation risk persists
watchItems.text: The US carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of November 3, even as Qatar-mediated peace talks continued. Trump called the operation 'not a war' and said a deal 'could happen,' while Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei spoke with Putin about strategic cooperation. Iran's Navy claimed an 11th oil tanker caught fire near the strait from a sea mine. The gap between diplomatic rhetoric and military reality remains wide — a failed negotiation could quickly restore the oil risk premium toward $115.

watchItems.title: US nonfarm payrolls — Friday, November 6
watchItems.text: The October jobs report lands Friday at 8:30 AM ET with a consensus forecast of 65K. A weak print could ease the December rate-hike probability from its current 87%, providing relief to rate-sensitive metals and crypto. A strong number would reinforce the higher-for-longer narrative. The ISM Manufacturing PMI came in strong at 55.5 for October, suggesting underlying economic resilience. September's unemployment rate was 4.2%. The report is the key macro input for the Fed's December 8–9 decision.

watchItems.title: Lithium carbonate tumbles to ¥93,800 — oversupply deepens
watchItems.text: Chinese lithium carbonate spot fell to ¥93,800 per tonne, down sharply from ¥97,500 earlier in the week. The decline extends the selloff from the mid-May peak above ¥200,000, driven by the SMM inventory restatement adding 175,000 tonnes to stockpile estimates, Australian mine restarts at Bald Hill and Finniss, the EU cap of 350,000 Chinese hybrid EV imports annually, and expectations of a growing surplus. Lithium futures on the Guangzhou exchange traded around ¥92,000. Goldman Sachs projects a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold had its most volatile session of the month on Wednesday, touching an intraday low of $3,893 before recovering to settle near $3,935. The wide $60 range reflected competing forces: election-day uncertainty supported safe-haven demand while strong ISM manufacturing data (55.5 in October) reinforced rate-hike expectations. The December rate-hike probability holds near 87% with NFP due Friday. The 2026 low of $3,876 set in late October continues to act as nearby support.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver eased to $49.85 on Wednesday, slipping back below the $50 level. The metal remains down about 19% on the month, reflecting persistent pressure from higher-for-longer rate expectations and a strong dollar. The gold-silver ratio widened slightly to approximately 78.9 as silver underperformed gold's intraday recovery.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: WTI $95.60 · Brent down 12% from last week's $117+ · Iran peace talks continue
desk.sum: Brent eased to $103.89 on Wednesday, down 1.4% as the Iran peace narrative continued to deflate the risk premium despite mixed signals on the ground. The US carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of November 3, but Trump said the operation was 'not a war' and that a deal 'could happen.' WTI slipped to $95.60. Iran's Navy claimed an 11th oil tanker caught fire near the strait from a sea mine. Brent is now down roughly 12% from last week's $117+ levels. OPEC+ holds December quotas unchanged; the November 29 session sets 2027 targets.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper eased to $6.41 per pound on Wednesday as risk appetite continued to pull back. LME copper fell 2% overnight on increased bearish positioning, while SHFE copper 2612 closed at 106,540 yuan per tonne, down 0.6%. Fundamentals remain tight — suppliers hold limited inventory and are reluctant to sell — but downstream buyers are cautious, purchasing only on a needs basis. SMM expects copper to consolidate in a narrow range near term.

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Under pressure from Hormuz peace hopes · YTD +34%
desk.sum: Newcastle coal edged lower to approximately $146 per tonne, continuing its decline as the prospect of a Hormuz reopening threatens to release Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG capacity. If Qatari LNG flows resume, coal-switching economics would weaken significantly in Asia and Europe. Year-to-date gains have compressed to roughly 34% from 36% earlier in the week. The March precedent — when coal fell below $130 on earlier Iran peace talks — suggests further downside if negotiations advance.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum fell 1.4% to approximately $1,437 on Wednesday, giving back Tuesday's bounce. The metal is now down about 16% on the month and well below its January record of $2,924. WPIC's 265,000-ounce surplus forecast for 2026 and the 87% December hike probability continue to weigh on the medium-term outlook. The declining oil price also dampens any diesel-catalyst demand expectations.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium fell 2.2% to approximately $940 on Wednesday, extending its decline to fresh 16-month lows. The metal is now down about 20% on the month, the worst performer on the desk. EV adoption and the shift toward platinum in catalytic converters continue to erode structural demand. Rate-hike expectations discourage investment flows into non-yielding metals. Nornickel's plant overhaul, expected to last into 2028, provides some supply-side support but is insufficient to offset the demand headwinds.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: ~10 transits/day vs 85 pre-war · US strikes Qeshm despite peace talks
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz situation grew more complex on Wednesday as the US carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island — located near the strait — even as Qatar-mediated peace talks continued. Iran described the exchanges as 'intensive' but Foreign Minister Araghchi said the ball is in Washington's court. Iran's Navy claimed an 11th oil tanker caught fire near the strait from a sea mine, contradicting US Central Command's assertion that main transit routes remain clear. Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Rezaei spoke with Putin about strategic cooperation. Approximately 10 transits per day versus 85 pre-war.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn fell to 442½¢, down 1.3% as harvest pressure mounted and the strong dollar continued to weigh on US export competitiveness. The grain is down about 11% on the month with managed money holding substantial short positions. Post-election trade policy uncertainty and Friday's NFP add to the cautious backdrop.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: December wheat eased to approximately 596¢ per bushel, extending what is now a tenth straight weekly loss. Ample global supply, resumed Russian grain shipments from Azov ports, and a strong dollar continue to weigh on prices. Record managed-money short positions and adequate world stocks cap any rally attempts. Winter wheat planting remains on schedule across the US Plains.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: Soybeans eased to approximately 1,200¢ per bushel, down 0.3% as harvest pressure and competitive Brazilian production continued to weigh. The grain is down about 6% on the month with the US crop running ahead of the five-year average. Chinese buying interest remains muted, and robust South American production estimates pressure the outlook.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin dipped to approximately $77,000 as post-Binance hack institutional outflows persisted and midterm election uncertainty weighed on risk appetite. BTC is defending the $76,000 level — the average cost basis of short-term holders — which analysts identify as the key support floor. Ethereum eased to $2,270. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen net outflows on most trading days since the Binance breach on October 29. The November 1 proof-of-reserves snapshot was scheduled but has not yet been published. Early midterm results showing Democrats winning the House could shift the crypto-regulatory outlook.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM ~$32 · TTF ~$31/MBtu · HH $2.91 · downside risk from Hormuz deal
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) eased to $31.70 per MMBtu, down 3.5% as the Iran peace narrative continued to weigh on forward expectations. If the Strait of Hormuz reopens, Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG capacity — diverted since early September — would flow back to Asian and European buyers, potentially compressing JKM toward the mid-$20s. European TTF holds near $31/MBtu. Henry Hub eased to $2.91.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait $765 · China domestic ¥7,200 · at risk from Hormuz deal
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,200 per tonne. The Iran peace talks represent the biggest potential catalyst for sulfur prices: a Hormuz reopening would release Middle East sulfur flows and rapidly ease the acute supply squeeze in fertilizer and mining supply chains. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). Chinese domestic sulfur is approximately 7,200 yuan per tonne.

desk.name: Potash
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367 per tonne. BPC settled a new India contract at $383 per tonne CFR, approximately $35 above China's 2026 benchmark. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. Seasonal Southern Hemisphere fertilizer demand provides modest support.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: Off 105k high · consolidating at lows since mid-Oct
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) continues to consolidate near 90,000 yuan per tonne after declining sharply from the 105,000-yuan October 9 high. SMM expects low-level sideways consolidation with supply still contracting under Document No. 46 export controls but demand remaining weak. A test below 90,000 remains possible if downstream activity does not improve.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, up over 130% since early 2025. China's Document No. 46 export controls retain a presumption of denial for US end users, and the Busan truce's Document No. 72 suspension has not meaningfully restored exports. China produces about 98% of global gallium. Supply diversification efforts remain in early stages.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Down from $5.44 in 2024 · steel demand soft
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds near $5.02 per pound, soft as steel demand weakens. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but the timing of large-scale adoption remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Rebounding from 4-week low · off $12,931 record · ICE inventories at 2.5-yr high
desk.sum: ICE cocoa recovered to approximately $5,419 per tonne, rebounding from the $5,374 four-week low. Rising ICE warehouse inventories — at a 2.5-year high of 3.69 million bags by late October — continue to cap rallies. StoneX projects 2026/27 global output to fall 9.6% to 4.74 million tonnes, which could turn the current surplus into a deficit. El Niño risks affecting West African producers into 2027 support the medium-term outlook.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.sum: Cobalt holds at approximately $33,510 per tonne, flat on the week and down about 14% on the month. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes per year through 2027 to support prices, but the EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP continues to structurally reduce demand. Glencore expects DRC exports to normalise in line with quotas.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Futures ~¥92k · down from ¥97.5k · halved from May ¥200k+
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate spot fell to ¥93,800 per tonne, down from ¥97,500 earlier in the week. The selloff continues from the mid-May peak above ¥200,000, driven by the SMM inventory restatement adding 175,000 tonnes to stockpile estimates, Australian mine restarts at Bald Hill and Finniss, an EU cap of 350,000 Chinese hybrid EV imports annually, and expectations of a growing surplus. Lithium futures on the Guangzhou exchange traded around ¥92,000. Goldman Sachs projects a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), little changed. Southeast Asian supply remains tight with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Auto-sector demand remains solid, supported by replacement-tyre cycles.
